To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

seizures were the presenting symptom in 10 of 81 children (12%) with a primary brain tumor, and that the diagnosis of a brain tumor in these children was delayed from the onset of the seizures by a median of 6 months.

seizures were the presenting clinical feature in 12% of children with brain tumours and that the majority had a focal seizure onset with a delay in diagnosis of 6 months from onset of the seizures to the final diagnosis of a brain tumour.
Seizures are the presenting symptom in 12% of children with brain tumours.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

seizures are a presenting symptom in 10% of children with brain tumours, that the most common tumours to present with seizures are low grade astrocytomas and that complete resection of the lesion results in seizure freedom.

seizures in children are not an unusual presentation of brain tumour, but that they are a late presentation and that a significant number of patients may become seizure free following complete resection of the lesion and/or adjuvant radiotherapy and/or adjuvent chemotherapy.
